story: The name is a portmanteau: 言葉 (kotoba, Japanese for “word”) + bạn (Vietnamese for “friend”), overlapping on the shared “ba” — carrying bạn's nặng tone mark. I was studying Japanese and Vietnamese at the same time and couldn't find one app that did spaced repetition, dictionary lookup, and reading practice the way I wanted. So I built it.

Kotoban is a multi-user progressive web app, currently in invite-only closed beta. It has a full design system — Ink & Lacquer, in light and dark — built mobile-first at 390px and scaled up. Under the hood it's FastAPI and SQLite on an Oracle Cloud box, with magic-link sign-in, invite requests, and an admin portal.

The content pipeline is the part I'm proudest of: vocabulary and reading material across twelve languages, generated and curated in batches, with audio throughout. It's the study tool I wished existed, and now it's the one I actually use.
tagline: A language-learning app I designed and built — currently in invite-only closed beta.
